text.offer: Morning, sleeper. Good, you're on your feet. Stuff's welling up out of the stream below the falls. Amber, slow, mean. Clear six of them off the banks before they get into the garden.
text.summary: Kill 6 amber oozes along the stream below the falls.
text.waiting: Still oozing? Then you're not done.
text.done: Six down. Not bad for your first day awake.

text.offer: Oh, you're up! Sit, sit. No, don't sit, I need you. Waking herb grows all round the abbey, pale little leaves. Steep them with honey, dear, never boil them, or they go bitter. Bring me six and I'll have a pot on for the next one through.
text.summary: Gather 6 waking herbs around the abbey.
text.waiting: Pale leaves, dear. Smell of rain.
text.done: Lovely. Smell that? That's what you woke up to.

text.offer: Those oozes Bryce is so cross about? Waste not, dear. A spoon of the stuff thickens a healing draught beautifully. Bottle five for me and you can have your pick of what I make with it.
text.summary: Bring 5 vials of amber ooze from the oozes by the stream.
text.waiting: Five vials, dear. Corked, if you can manage it.
text.done: Oh, still warm. Take your pick, and mind you drink it before it drinks you. A joke, dear.

text.offer: Hornets have nested in the brush west of the stream, down the glen. Seven nests last I counted. Get a smudge going under four of them and they'll move on. Don't stand there admiring it.
text.summary: Smoke out 4 hornet nests west of the stream.
text.waiting: Four nests, sleeper. Smoke, not stares.
text.done: That's the stuff. You'll get stung less tomorrow.

text.offer: Four bundles. Candles, bread, bandages. Gone from the stores in the night, and I counted them twice. Thieves are camped by a lean-to at the glen's mouth. Bring back four and I'll stop counting.
text.summary: Bring back 4 bundles of Abbey Stores from the thieves at the glen's mouth.
text.done: Four. Fine. I'll mark them back in.

text.offer: Kobolds. Runts, up by the falls, west of the path. Kobolds live under the hills, not up here. Something's chased them out, and I don't like it. Thin them out. Eight should send a message.
text.summary: Kill 8 kobold runts west of the falls path.
text.waiting: Eight, sleeper. Count them as you go.
text.done: Good. Now I want to know what they were running from.

text.offer: The lanterns round the falls have gone out. ... It is thin here, where you woke. Thin like ice in spring. The light keeps the next sleeper from waking in the dark. Light four of them for me.
text.summary: Relight 4 lanterns around the foot of the falls.
text.done: There. Listen. The falls sound softer when they're lit.

text.offer: Something lies under the cliff, west of the runts. A small body. A pick beside it. ... Bryce wants to know what drove them. The dead keep their reasons close. Go and look.
text.summary: Search the dead kobold under the cliff west of the runts' camp.
text.waiting: ... You haven't looked yet. I can tell.
text.done: Mine dust, and grave dirt under its claws. They dug into something old.

text.offer: I was coming back up from the vale and, sorry, I'm still shaking. A man followed me. A dead man. He's wandering at the glen's mouth now. I couldn't, I didn't... Would you put him to rest? He had a ring. I'd like to know whose.
text.summary: Put down the dead man at the glen's mouth and bring back his ring.
text.waiting: Is he still... sorry. Is he still there?
text.done: Barrow bronze. He came up from the old barrow fields. Sorry. Thank you. Sorry.

text.offer: Mine dust and grave dirt. So they broke into something down there and ran. Fine. They've still got a leader up by the falls, a rock-caller. Take it down and the rest will scatter home.
text.summary: Kill the kobold geomancer leading the runts above the falls.
text.waiting: Leader's still standing. Go fix that.
text.done: That's the glen clear. You've earned your legs, sleeper.

text.offer: The lanterns are lit. Now you can go back, a little way. ... Sit by the stone at the pool. Close your eyes. Don't be afraid of what looks back.
text.summary: Rest by the stone at the falls pool.
text.waiting: ... Not yet. The stone is waiting.
text.done: You saw it, then. Don't tell me. It's yours. ... It will make sense, later.

text.offer: Every sleeper leaves us eventually, and I find I mind it less each time, which is either wisdom or age. Edric Ashby farms at the foot of the glen. He's had kobolds at his stores, and something under his hill. Go and see him. Tell him the abbot sent you, and watch him sigh.
text.summary: Speak with Edric Ashby at Ashby farm, south of the glen.
text.done: The abbot sent you? Course he did. Well, you've got two hands. That'll do.

text.offer: Tam tells me you brought back a ring from the barrow fields, and that a dead man wore it. I'd rather it were neither. Father Wren in Lakeford reads old marks better than I do, and worries more usefully. Take it to him, if you would.
text.summary: Take the burial ring to Father Aldous Wren in Lakeford.
text.done: A barrow mark, and a wearer who walked. Let me see. ... No. Sit a moment. I will need to look this up properly.

text.offer: Every night, kobolds. Out of the old mine on the hill, into my stores, and off with a sack each. Six sacks gone this week. They camp round the mine's mouth now, bold as crows. Get my grain back.
text.summary: Bring back 6 Sacks of Ashby Grain from the kobolds at the old mine's mouth.
text.done: Six. Good. Now, why are kobolds coming out of a mine they spent forty years digging? Something's wrong in there.

text.offer: Kobolds don't leave a mine they've dug. Something drove them out. Go in, past the work rooms, down the deep tunnel at the end of the gallery, and see what. Then come and tell me so I can stop guessing.
text.summary: Go into the old mine and reach the deep tunnel at the end of the gallery.
text.done: Skeletons. Fighting the kobolds. In my hill. ... Go and tell Mother. No, really. She'll want to say she told me so, and she might as well get it over with.

text.offer: Mother's in the house. She knows the old stories, and she'll make you sit through all of them. Ask her about the hill.
text.summary: Speak with Gran Ashby at the farmhouse.
text.done: So. The kobolds dug into the barrow. Course they did. Sit down, child, this'll take a while.

text.offer: There was a chieftain buried under that hill, with his spears and his people round him. If his dead are up, he's up. The rest follow him. Go through the mine to the barrow's round room and put him down, child. Then come back and I'll teach you the rest.
text.summary: Kill the Barrow Lord in the barrow beyond the old mine's deep tunnel.
text.waiting: He's still up. I can feel it in my knees.
text.done: Down? Good. Now it needs closing, or something will only wake him again.

text.offer: My gran's rite. Salt, ash and a word. Take this to the altar stone in the barrow's room, scatter it, and say the word. It closes a grave so it stays closed. ... It shouldn't have opened in the first place, child. Something's been calling to the dead round here. This one, I can shut.
text.summary: Consecrate the altar stone in the barrow beyond the old mine.
text.waiting: Is it done? You'd know if it was done.
text.done: It's shut. I felt it go. But there's more of them, child, all over the vale, and they're not waking on their own. Something's calling them. Go to Lakeford, to the priest. Tell him an old woman says so.

text.offer: The rats in the south field are big as dogs. Bigger than Bet's dog was, anyway. Kill eight and I'll call you nearly as good as me. Over the stream, past the bridge.
text.summary: Kill 8 giant rats in the Ashbys' south field.
text.done: Eight? Hm. That's fine. I'd have done nine.

text.offer: Da won't go near the barrow in the south fields. Dead men walking round it, I've seen them. Go and knock six down, and then tell the priest in Lakeford, Father Wren. Somebody ought to know who'll do something.
text.summary: Destroy 6 zombies round the Ashby barrow, then tell Father Wren in Lakeford.
text.done: Rowan Ashby sent you? Then it's true. Sit a moment. Let me find the right book.

text.offer: They come through the gap in the hills, north-west of here. Every few nights. Go up there and teach them the way back. Eight of their raiders should do it.
text.summary: Kill 8 bandit raiders at the hill gap, north-west of Westhill.
text.done: Quiet last night. First time in a month. Sit. There's stew.

text.offer: They took the seed corn. No seed, no spring. They hold it at their huts in the woods north of here, on the hill. Bring back five sacks.
text.summary: Bring back 5 Sacks of Seed Corn from the bandits north of Westhill.
text.done: Five. Good. There was a letter in one of these. Read it.

text.offer: Fence on the north side's down where they came through. Lumber's piled by it. Stand the panels back up. Five will do. I'd do it myself, but somebody has to watch the gap.
text.summary: Mend 5 broken fence panels on Westhill's north side.
text.done: Good work. Square, too. You've done this before.

text.offer: I was picking up windfalls in the old trees, west, past the barn. I filled six baskets. Then the bandits came and I ran and left them. Can you get them? Ma will be cross about the baskets.
text.summary: Fetch 6 baskets of windfall apples from the trees west of Westhill.
text.waiting: Did you find them? Were the bandits there?
text.done: All six! Ma, look! ... She's not looking. She's pleased though. That's her pleased face.

text.offer: Bandits off the hills hit my sister's place harder than mine. Westhill, under the hills, west down the trail and south. She won't ask me for help. She'll take yours. Don't tell her I sent you. ... Tell her I sent you.
text.summary: Go to Westhill farmstead and speak with Marta Coyle.
text.done: Edric sent you. Hm. Sit. Eat first.

text.offer: Report. Dead men at the town's west edge, three nights running. My lads won't go near. Bring me six of their bones, and I'll take them to Father Wren, so he'll stop telling me it's my imagination. ... No. You take them to him. I've a town to watch.
text.summary: Bring 6 Risen Bones from the dead at Lakeford's western edge to Father Wren.
text.done: The sergeant sent you? Then it isn't only the Ashbys' fields. Let me see them. Ah.

text.offer: The old barrows were sealed with a door stone, and the rites say the stone falls outward only when the dead push it. Go to the Ashby barrow, north-west of here in the fields, and look at its door stone. Tell me which way it fell.
text.summary: Examine the door stone of the Ashby barrow.
text.done: Outward. Then they were called, and they came out on their own feet. 'What is buried keeps, until it is called.' Someone is calling.

text.offer: Earth remembers what passes through it. If I have earth from another barrow, I can read which way the calling comes from. The Southwood barrow lies south-west, in the woods past the boar fields. Bring me five pouches of its earth, from the mounds round its door.
text.summary: Gather 5 Pouches of Barrow Earth at the Southwood barrow.
text.done: Cold. Feel it. ... It pulls. North-east, toward the hills past the river.

text.offer: Edric Ashby ordered a keg a week ago and hasn't been in for it, because Edric Ashby won't come within a mile of anyone who might mention his sister. Take it up to him, would you? North-west up the road. Tell him it's paid for. It isn't.
text.summary: Take the Keg of Merriweather Ale to Edric Ashby at Ashby farm.
text.done: Bess's ale? Finally. Paid for? ... It isn't, is it.

text.offer: My stew's famous. My stew is also out of venison. The stags graze in the meadows north of Ashby's, under the hills. Six haunches, and you eat free tonight.
text.summary: Bring 6 Haunches of Venison from the stags in the meadows north of Ashby farm.
text.waiting: Smell that? That's stew without venison. Sad stew.
text.done: Lovely. Sit down, you've earned a bowl. Two bowls.

text.offer: Frogmen. On the north-east shore of the lake. Never come this far inland. Not in my time. Kill eight. Then I'll know they can be killed, and so will my lads.
text.summary: Kill 8 frogmen on the lake's north-east shore.
text.done: Eight. Good. They're scouting. For what, I don't know. Saltwick might.

text.offer: Weir's down. Where the river leaves the lake, east of the dock. Posts are knocked flat. Stand five back up. ... Lake gives what it gives. Weir helps.
text.summary: Set 5 of the fish weir's posts upright where the river leaves the lake.
text.done: Hm. Good. Fish tonight.

text.offer: Eight bear claws. South wood, south-west of town, past the boar fields. The black bears there are big as a cart. Bigger. You bring the claws, I win the bet, I buy you a drink with Bess's money. Everyone wins but Bess.
text.summary: Bring 8 Bear Claws from the black bears in the south wood.
text.done: Eight! Bess! BESS! Pay up!

text.offer: Saltwick's on the coast, south down the road past the woods. Agna, our harbourmaster, she sent me for fighters. Please go. Tell her Lise sent you, and that I'm coming back as soon as I've stopped shaking.
text.summary: Go to Saltwick and speak with Harbourmaster Agna Stroud.
text.done: Lise found someone. Good. I'll take you.

text.offer: Fennick's Landing went quiet a month ago. West along the shore, past the river mouth. We've seen smoke, then nothing. Go and look for anyone left. I'm not hopeful. Go anyway.
text.summary: Search the ruins of Fennick's Landing, west along the shore past the river mouth.
text.done: None. ... I'll tell them. No. You've done enough. I'll tell them.

text.offer: There'll be things. In the houses, in the boats. Small things people kept. Bring what you can find. Six, if there are six. Someone should have them.
text.summary: Bring back 6 of Fennick's Keepsakes from the ruins of Fennick's Landing.
text.done: This was Morwen's. ... Thank you. I'll see the others get the rest.

text.offer: They gather west of the barricade every evening, along the dunes, and come at us after dark. Break their line before they're ready. Ten will do. Twenty would be better.
text.summary: Kill 10 frogmen at the siege line west of Saltwick.
text.done: Quiet last night. First quiet night in a month. We'll sleep in shifts.

objectives.text: Frogmen hunters killed at the siege line

text.offer: The wet ones carry these. Shell, bone, kelp. Same marks on every one. Somebody makes them. Bring me six from the raiders, west by the river or east past the point, and I'll tell you who.
text.summary: Bring 6 Frogman Totems from the frogmen raiders west or east of Saltwick.
text.done: Same marks. A caller. A tidecaller, the old fishers said, though I thought it was a story. He'll be on the shore somewhere, far west, away from the fighting.

text.offer: Kett says there's one who calls them. Far west on the shore, past the ruins, a few huts on the sand. Kill him, and they've no reason to come back. Kill him, and I'll stop counting every morning.
text.summary: Kill Murk-Eye the Tidecaller at his huts on the shore far west of Saltwick.
text.done: Then it's done. Forty-one people. I counted this morning. I'll count tomorrow too, but I'll sleep first.

text.offer: Crab, dearie. The strand west of the ruins, past the tidecaller's huts if you're brave and before them if you're sensible. Eight crabs' worth. I'll make a soup that'll put meat on Agna, if she'd ever sit down to eat it.
text.summary: Bring 8 Strand Crab Meat from the sand crabs on the strand far west of Saltwick.
text.done: Lovely. Lovely! Sit. Sit. Eat.

text.offer: There was a letter in the seed. Orders, signed. They mention Riverwatch. Take it to the captain there, east of Lakeford over the river. Bandits don't sign things. Somebody's leading them.
text.summary: Take the bandits' signed orders to Captain Ravel at Riverwatch.
text.done: Signed. 'D.M.' And a note of our patrol times. Someone's been watching us.

text.offer: Bandits on the road south-west of here, in the autumn wood. They hit a cart yesterday. In daylight. Insulting. Clear twelve off the road and I'll stop being insulted.
text.summary: Kill 12 bandits on the Riverwatch road in the autumn wood.
text.done: Better. Much better. Now, where do they sleep?

text.offer: Their camp's deeper in, south-east, on the rise. Someone in that camp keeps accounts. Bandits who sign orders keep ledgers. Find it.
text.summary: Search the autumn wood bandit camp for their ledger.
text.done: Payments to 'the chief'. And a drop point. West of here, between the woods and the Saltwick road. That's where he hides.

text.offer: Dace Merrin. 'D.M.' The ledger names him. He hides west of the autumn wood, in a barn off the Saltwick road. End this. Then tell the farms in the west they can sleep.
text.summary: Kill Dace Merrin, the bandit chief, at his hideout west of the autumn wood.
text.done: Then the road's ours again. Thank you. And tell the Westhill widow. She'll pretend not to care.

text.offer: The earth pulls north-east, toward the hills past the river. Captain Ravel at Riverwatch watches that country. Ask him whether he has seen anything. Lights, perhaps. Things that walk at night.
text.summary: Ask Captain Ravel at Riverwatch about the hills north-west of the fort.
text.done: Lights? Every night. Round the broken tower. Ranger Marsh can tell you more.

text.offer: River barrow's north of here, up the river. Dead coming out of it for weeks. Some of them wear charms. New ones. Bring me one and let's see who made it.
text.summary: Bring a Ritual Charm from the dead at the river barrow north of Riverwatch.
text.done: New wire, old bone. Someone made this last month. It points at the broken tower. Of course it does.

text.offer: Marsh says there are stones in the hills round the tower, with fires by them. A circle. Break it. Topple the stones. Five of them. Whatever he's doing up there, he can't do it without them.
text.summary: Topple 5 ritual stones on the hills round the broken tower.
text.done: Lights are fainter tonight. Good. Now he'll know we're coming.

text.offer: He's in the tower. Go up there and end it. And bring back whatever he's written. Men like that always write it down.
text.summary: Kill the necromancer in the broken tower and bring back his journal.
text.done: Dead. Good. That journal, though. That's Father Wren's to read, not mine.

text.offer: Take it to Lakeford. To the priest. He'll want it more than he'll want to read it.
text.summary: Take Crale's Journal to Father Wren in Lakeford.
text.done: 'The Eye beneath Thornwood.' ... There are more of them. Not here. In Thornwood, beyond the hills. This isn't over, my friend. This was one of them.

text.offer: Riverwatch's dead are buried outside their wall, and Captain Ravel asked me for salt to bless their graves. Will you take it? East, along the road, over the river.
text.summary: Take the Blessed Salt to Captain Ravel at Riverwatch.
text.done: Wren's salt. Good. My lads will sleep better. So will the ones outside the wall.

text.offer: Spiders in the east wood. North-west of here, past the road. Big ones. Their silk makes bowstrings that hold in the rain. Six bundles? Please?
text.summary: Bring 6 Spider Silk from the cave spiders in the east wood.
text.done: Oh, that's lovely. Look how it shines. Thank you. Thank you!

text.offer: Going north? Take the road up past the lake, all the way. Greyspur Gate. Tell Warden Stell that Benno says he's resting very hard. He'll know what that means. It means I'm not.
text.summary: Go north to Greyspur Gate and speak with Warden Stell.
text.done: Benno. Resting. Hm.

text.offer: Trogs. East, in the foothills. Kill ten.
text.summary: Kill 10 trog bashers in the foothills east of Greyspur Gate.
text.done: Good.

text.offer: Beacon on the west ridge. Out since the storm. Light it. Greyspur watches for it.
text.summary: Light the signal beacon on the ridge west of the gate.
text.done: Greyspur will see it. Good. Go up when you're ready. They'll know you're coming.

text.offer: There's an old working on the slope west of the yard, the mine with the timber mouth. Lumps of ore lying all round it that nobody's bothered to pick up. Bring me six. I want to know what's in this mountain before I go up it.
text.summary: Gather 6 lumps of ore round the old mine mouth west of the gate's yard.
text.done: Look at that grain. Iron, and something brighter in it. Greyspur iron. I knew it.
